I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou, this is the safest way for me to make grain and avoid taking too much market risk. I know this system, I can manage it with the labor I have, and it fits the local water and weather conditions. So I will harvest the winter wheat first, then plant summer maize right after. I will not spread myself across many crops. I would rather do two familiar crops well than chase a higher price and carry more risk.

For winter wheat, I will stay with an improved variety, not old seed I save myself. I want stable yield, better stand, and more even maturity. I will use rotary tillage before wheat, put on enough nitrogen as the main fertilizer, and give phosphorus and potassium too because I do not want weak roots or poor grain filling. I will irrigate about three times if water is available: once at overwintering or before winter if the soil is dry, once around jointing, and once around grain filling. I will spray mainly for weeds and then for disease or aphids if pressure shows up. I will manage the field simply and on time.

After wheat harvest, I will go straight into summer maize. I will use hybrid maize because I care about yield and strong ears. I will keep tillage light and mostly no-till after wheat so I can save time and catch soil moisture. I will put most nitrogen around the big feeding stage instead of all at once, and I will still give phosphorus and potassium so the crop does not run short later. I will irrigate fewer times than wheat, mainly depending on rain, but I will not let it suffer badly at the key stages. I will spray if I see weeds early and insects later. My goal is steady grain output, manageable work, and lower risk.
